candidate.answerReason: P^{2n}Q^m=(2^m)^{2n}(3^n)^m=2^{2mn}3^{mn}=12^{mn} for all integers m and n.

methods.label: Rewrite using bases 2 and 3
methods.explanation:
Since \(P\) and \(Q\) are powers of 2 and 3, rewrite \(12=2^2\cdot3\) using those same bases. The power-of-a-product and power-of-a-power rules give
\[
\begin{aligned}
12^{mn}
&=(2^2\cdot3)^{mn}\\
&=2^{2mn}3^{mn}\\
&=(2^m)^{2n}(3^n)^m\\
&=P^{2n}Q^m.
\end{aligned}
\]
All bases involved are positive, so these rules remain valid when either integer exponent is zero or negative. Thus the expression is \(P^{2n}Q^m\), choice E.
methods.levelReason: Only integer-exponent laws are used, including their ordinary extension to zero and negative exponents.
